summary: All five smoke gates green after one tests retry; the wave's three edits are correct and minimal. biome.json ignore-list additions surgically fix the prior F-003/F-005 scope miss without affecting apps/ or packages/ lint coverage. apps/api/src/modules/auth/schema.ts is a pure biome --write reformat (import-order + line-width) with zero semantic change; flagged as info because target_files arrays are empty and infra-builder is editing under apps/api/src/**. vitest.config.ts singleFork is correctly scoped to the integration project; however the underlying testcontainer reuse race surfaced in Phase 1 retry, so a high finding records the residual fragility for the retro.

findings.summary: Vitest singleFork mitigates but does not eliminate testcontainer withReuse() teardown race; tests flaked on first run
findings.evidence: Phase 1 attempt 1 failed in auth.constant-time.test.ts with docker-modem '(HTTP code 404) no such container' from stopPostgresContainer at line 82 (container.stop()), then cascade TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading pool)' because beforeAll never assigned testDb. Root cause: every integration file (11 total) calls stopPostgresContainer in afterAll, but startPostgresContainer (line 37: builder.withReuse()) shares a single docker container handle across files. Even with vitest.config.ts singleFork (this wave) serialising fork lifetime, the FIRST file to finish calls container.stop() and subsequent files race against a now-removed container.
findings.recommendation: Move container start/stop to a globalSetup/globalTeardown (Vitest globalSetup option) so the reused container is started ONCE per process and stopped ONCE at the very end. Files would call only reset() between tests, never stop(). Alternative: drop .withReuse() and rely on singleFork (each file gets its own container). Track in the sprint retro and add a verification_failure_modes entry for `pnpm -r test` with flake_rate ~0.5 so the next reviewer can retry under R3 with provenance.

findings.summary: biome.json edited but wave task.target_files arrays are all empty (scope drift signal)
findings.evidence: wave-smoke task `task-smoke` declares target_files: { create:[], update:[], remove:[], may_also_touch:[] }. biome.json was modified to add .relay/**, .planning/**, .claude/**, scripts/** to files.ignore. Edit is correct (resolves prior wave-smoke F-003/F-005) but is technically scope drift per code-reviewing R4.2 because the smoke task contract has no target_files allowance.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for a smoke wave whose task is by-definition cross-cutting; document the convention in sprint-planning skill that smoke-wave tasks may have a non-empty may_also_touch covering config files needed to make gates green (biome.json, vitest config, lockfiles).

findings.summary: infra-builder edited apps/api/src/modules/auth/schema.ts (typically forbidden); diff confirmed cosmetic-only
findings.evidence: Builder is infra-builder; the file is under apps/api/src/** which the infra-builder persona forbids. Diff inspection (lines 1-10): the single import statement was reformatted by biome (organizeImports + 100-char line-width) from one line to a 9-line block. Symbol set is byte-identical (relations, sql from drizzle-orm; type AnyPgColumn, check, customType, pgTable, text, timestamp, uuid from drizzle-orm/pg-core). No added or removed imports, no logic change. Build and tests pass.
findings.recommendation: Accept as a side-effect of biome --write running during the smoke gate green-up. If the team wants persona purity, run `biome check` (read-only) instead of `--write` in builder personas other than feature-builder; or pre-format the file via a one-off chore wave before locking down persona scopes.

findings.summary: vitest.config.ts edited but wave task.target_files arrays are all empty (scope drift signal)
findings.evidence: Same root cause as F-002: smoke task contract has empty target_files, but the wave needed a config tweak (lines 27-32: pool='forks', poolOptions.forks.singleFork=true on the integration project only) to satisfy the tests gate. Change is correctly scoped to the integration project (unit project at lines 6-15 retains default parallelism).
findings.recommendation: Same as F-002 — formalise smoke-wave latitude for config files in sprint-planning skill.

findings.summary: biome.json ignores scripts/** wholesale; future scripts will receive zero lint coverage
findings.evidence: Added "scripts/**" to files.ignore. The repo has top-level scripts/ for relay tooling (commit-sdlc-init.sh, wave-commit.sh, open-pr.sh, validate-review.mjs, etc.). All-glob ignore means any future JS/TS in scripts/ silently skips lint.
findings.recommendation: Narrow to "scripts/**/*.sh" if only shell scripts need exclusion, or split: ignore relay-tooling subdirs explicitly, lint hand-authored Node scripts. Low priority — current scripts are mostly .sh and .mjs that pre-date biome adoption.
